assumptions: Responsibility for soundness and record keeping carries a substantive performance component when read with the express requirement to ensure proper records and compatibility.
The text does not establish strict liability for every incident or an absolute guarantee against failure.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

deferred.22174c64a9d2bb1c3da83ec8.distinction: Unlike the allocation-focused reading, this reading requires evidence of satisfactory substantive performance to conclude that paragraph 10 itself is fulfilled. Authority and diligent supervision are relevant but cannot substitute for the required operational and record-keeping condition.
questions: What operational and record-keeping condition counts as satisfactory, and how do incidents, duration and remediation affect that assessment?
Is the governing standard outcome-based, conduct-based, or a combination?
deferred.22174c64a9d2bb1c3da83ec8.statement: Read substantively with the requirement to ensure proper ownership records and operational compatibility, paragraph 10 requires retained accountability exercised so that management, operations and record keeping meet the applicable standard. A fulfillment conclusion would require evidence of retained authority, effective supervisory conduct and satisfactory operational and record-keeping performance. The excerpts do not supply a complete standard or facts permitting that conclusion.
deferred.22174c64a9d2bb1c3da83ec8.subject: Paragraph 10 and footnote 1: substantive fulfillment

assumptions: Footnote 5's unqualified direction to confirm and demonstrate creates a minimum demonstration duty independently of a request.
Paragraph 14's request qualification continues to govern its broader or specifically requested demonstration; this reconciliation is uncertain.

citations.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.
Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.distinction: On this rival reading, no request is needed for the footnote's minimum demonstration. Its strongest weakness is that it reduces the apparent effect of paragraph 14's express request qualification. Footnote 5 does not similarly remove the independent request conditions in paragraphs 15 and 16.

facts.meaning: The assessed actor and tokenisation arrangement fall within the Product Provider duties in paragraph 14 and footnote 5.
facts.name: provider_in_scope

facts.meaning: The SFC has made a request applicable to the assessed Product Provider and arrangement for the paragraph 14 demonstration.
facts.name: demonstration_requested

questions: Can the unqualified footnote impose a standing minimum demonstration while the main paragraph makes demonstration request-dependent?
Does paragraph 14's SFC satisfaction standard govern this standing minimum, and when must it be provided?
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] For an in-scope Product Provider, true means a minimum demonstration is called for under paragraph 14 and footnote 5 regardless of whether a request exists; false does not arise within this reading's scope. This is an obligation-activation predicate, not a finding of fulfillment. Footnote 5 independently requires confirmation and demonstration to the SFC of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and the specified smart-contract assurance. Read together with paragraph 14, SFC satisfaction plausibly governs the demonstration, while the reach of high confidence remains unresolved. Without a request, this minimum duty persists; paragraphs 15 and 16 do not activate their respective requirements to obtain third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion.
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.subject: Paragraph 14 demonstration trigger with an independent footnote 5 minimum

deferred.22174c64a9d2bb1c3da83ec8.question: Has the Product Provider fulfilled paragraph 10's substantive responsibility requirement through retained accountability, effective supervision and operational and ownership-record performance meeting the applicable standard, read with the proper-records and operational-compatibility requirement?
deferred.22174c64a9d2bb1c3da83ec8.unit_of_assessment: One Product Provider's substantive discharge of responsibility for one tokenisation arrangement and associated ownership records.
deferred.22174c64a9d2bb1c3da83ec8.temporal_basis: During the assessment period for continuing responsibility; incident duration, remediation and the assessment period remain unspecified.
deferred.22174c64a9d2bb1c3da83ec8.true_means: The combined substantive requirement is fulfilled under this rival reading. Authority or diligent supervision alone is insufficient; the text does not establish an absolute guarantee against every incident.
deferred.22174c64a9d2bb1c3da83ec8.false_means: The substantive responsibility requirement is not met under the applicable standard; missing facts or an unidentified standard leave the answer unresolved, not automatically false.

deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.unit_of_assessment: Activation of footnote 5's minimum demonstration duty for one Product Provider and tokenisation arrangement.
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.temporal_basis: At assessment, while within scope; activation is unconditional on a request, but the excerpt supplies no performance deadline.
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.true_means: Minimum demonstration of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and the specified high-confidence smart-contract assurance is called for. Paragraphs 15 and 16 retain their separate request conditions.
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.false_means: False does not arise within scope under this reading. Being outside scope is not a finding of nonperformance.
